## Visualizing Function Transformations

In this R script, we visualize the transformations of the quadratic function  
\\( f(x) = x^2 \\).  

We demonstrate:
**Vertical and horizontal contractions**  

Each transformation is shown on the same plot for comparison.  
By observing these transformations, we can understand how parameters affect the graph’s shape and position.

```{r transformations, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load required library
library(ggplot2)

# Define the base function
f <- function(x) x^2

# Create a sequence of x values
x <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 400)

# Compute transformations
data <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  base = f(x),
  vertical_contraction = 0.5 * f(x), # contract vertically
  horizontal_contraction = f(2 * x) # contract horizontally
)

# Reshape data for plotting
library(tidyr)
data_long <- pivot_longer(
  data,
  cols = -x,
  names_to = "transformation",
  values_to = "y"
)

# Assign custom labels for clarity
labels <- c(
  base = "Base",
  vertical_contraction = "Vertical Contraction (×0.5)",
  horizontal_contraction = "Horizontal Contraction (×0.5)"
)

# Plot all transformations
ggplot(data_long, aes(x = x, y = y, color = transformation)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "base" = "black",
    "vertical_contraction" = "orange",
    "horizontal_contraction" = "gold"
  ),
  labels = labels
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Transformations of the Function y = x²",
    subtitle = "Demonstrating Shifts, Stretches, and Contractions",
    x = "x",
    y = "y",
    color = "Transformation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```
